title: Computer Use in Gemini 3.5 Flash
hook: DeepMind put computer-use agents — reading the screen, then clicking, typing, and scrolling through real UIs — into its fast, low-cost Flash tier.
key_points: Computer use lets the model operate software like a person: it sees the screen, then issues clicks, keystrokes, and scrolls to finish a task.
Shipping it in the Flash tier targets the per-action speed and cost that long, multi-step UI workflows demand.
Browser and app navigation becomes an API capability rather than a one-off research demo.
It extends the agent loop from text and tool calls to direct control of graphical interfaces.
content_html: Google DeepMind brought "computer use" to Gemini 3.5 Flash — the model's fast, low-cost tier. Computer use means the model can operate software the way a person does: it looks at the screen, then clicks buttons, types into fields, and scrolls to carry out a task, instead of only calling predefined tools.
extra_html:
What it is

A computer-use agent runs in a loop: observe the current screen, decide the next action, perform it, then observe again. That turns browser and application navigation into something the model drives end to end, rather than a workflow a developer has to script step by step. Putting it in the Flash tier — built for speed and low cost — is the notable part, because long UI tasks chain together many model calls.

Why it matters

Most real automation work is many small steps, not one big prompt, so the economics of each action matter as much as raw capability. Offering computer use in a cheap, fast tier pushes GUI automation closer to something you can run at production scale. See DeepMind's announcement for capabilities and availability.

related.title: Gemini 3.1 Pro: Frontier Reasoning (2026)
related.hook: Gemini 3.1 Pro pushes core reasoning past the Gemini 3 Pro baseline, scoring 77.1% verified on ARC-AGI-2 - a benchmark built to resist the memorization that inflates other scores.

related.title: ReAct: Reasoning + Acting
related.hook: Thinking alone can drift; acting alone is blind. ReAct interleaves reasoning with tool calls so an LLM can plan, look things up, and correct course — the template for agents.

related.title: Model Context Protocol (MCP): A Standard for Connecting LLMs to Tools
related.hook: MCP is an open protocol that standardizes how AI applications expose tools, data, and resources to models - think USB-C for AI tool integrations.

related.title: Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber
related.hook: Google splits its fast tier three ways: a workhorse that answers in fewer tokens, a 350-tokens-per-second speed model, and a security specialist locked behind a government pilot.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'computer use' let a model do that plain tool-calling does not?
flashcards.back_html: Operate graphical software directly — read the screen and click, type, and scroll — instead of only calling predefined functions or APIs.

flashcards.prompt: Why ship computer use in the fast, low-cost Flash tier specifically?

choices.text: Multi-step UI workflows make many model calls, so per-action speed and cost dominate the bill
Flash is the only Gemini tier able to process images
Smaller models are inherently safer to give control of a computer

flashcards.explanation_html: A task that takes dozens of screen-read-then-act steps multiplies the cost and latency of each call, so a cheap, fast tier is what makes the capability practical.
